chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad, from Imran ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from some of our companions, who attributed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The camel-drivers and the caravan-leaders, when the journey becomes arduous for them, should shorten (the prayer) between the two stations and complete (it) at the station."

key_terms.جَدَّ بِهِمَا السَّيْرُ: when the journey becomes arduous/hard for them

ai.seo_question: When should travelers shorten their prayers during an arduous journey according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical application of *qasr* (shortening prayer) by linking the permissibility to the physical hardship of the journey, specifically citing the fatigue of camel drivers and caravan leaders. It establishes a nuanced legal principle where the ease of reaching a resting place (*manzil*) allows for the completion of the prayer, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on removing undue burden (*raf' al-haraj*) during travel.
